Ava (eng-infra): Heads up — seeing a big spike in dropped pod connections in westus2 GPU pool since kernel update at 03:10 UTC. Multiple jobs failing with gRPC broken streams.
Rajat (eng-platform): Uh oh. Symptoms? packet loss, timeouts, or kube-proxy errors?
Ava (eng-infra): kube-proxy log shows connection resets and we have kernel dmesg: 
```
  nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet.
  nf_conntrack: can't insert conntrack entry, hash full
  kernel: nf_conntrack: dropped packet
```
Also saw lots of short-lived SNAT entries (ephemeral port churn) from inter-pod east-west traffic when RDMA fell back to TCP.
Samira (eng-sre): @Ava can you paste `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` and `nf_conntrack_max`? Also any MTU changes? RoCE needs jumbo frames.
Ava (eng-infra): Count ~ 262K, max 262144. So we hit the limit. MTU on pods is 9000, but host NIC got reverted to 1500 on some nodes after the kernel package rolled which fragmented RoCE handshakes. That pushed RDMA -> TCP fallback, creating thousands of short TCP connections per job.
Liam (eng-ml): That explains why model serving jobs show connection churn — every KV cache refill opens many ephemeral connections.
Rajat (eng-platform): Repro steps? can we push a canary config to disable masquerade for pod->pod intra-node traffic? Calico has `ipip`/`masquerade` options we can tune.
Ava (eng-infra): Trying a quick workaround: increased `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` to 524288 on the nodes and tuned `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` to 86400. Doing it via ssh bootstrap daemonset now.
Samira (eng-sre): +1 for temporary knob, but that's a bandaid. Need root cause: why MTU changed and why RDMA sessions failed. Possible kernel regression with RDMA driver after update.
Rajat (eng-platform): Also consider enabling conntrack hashsize change early in boot to avoid rehash cost (`sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_buckets=131072`). Add node sysctl to ASG image.
Ava (eng-infra): Noted. Also rolling back the host kernel on two problematic AZs to previous build — testing now.
deploy-bot: rolling-deploy started: rollback-host-kernel-westus2-azb -> 6 nodes (in progress)
Liam (eng-ml): Quick cost note — we had autoscaler add 18 preemptible GPU nodes during the spike. If this repeats we'll burn ~$7k/day extra. We should throttle scale-up on transient errors.
Samira (eng-sre): Agreed. Add a policy to ignore short-lived pod failures tied to `connection reset` for 10m before scaling.
Rajat (eng-platform): Action items: 1) keep conntrack_max bump as temporary, 2) investigate kernel RDMA regression, 3) ensure MTU uniformity across NICs and CNI, 4) add non-masquerade rule for intra-cluster pod traffic where possible, 5) add autoscaler backoff for conn churn.
Ava (eng-infra): I'll keep the bumped sysctls for 6 hours and monitor. Will post numbers in ~20m. :eyes:
Samira (eng-sre): Thanks — if we still see spikes after rollback, we'll open an incident and gather perf traces.
Ava (eng-infra): Current status (05:05 UTC): conntrack_count dropped to 38K after rollback on 6 nodes. GRPC errors reduced. Marking as mitigated for now.
Rajat (eng-platform): Great. Please add a follow-up RFC for long-term fixes (CNI MASQ rules, image with conntrack tuning, autoscaler backoff).
Ava (eng-infra): Will do.
